title: PodcastsIPadView
description: Create AggregatorApp/iPad/Podcasts/PodcastsIPadView.swift. 2-column layout (no supplementary column): episode list in content column; PodcastPlayerView in detail column driven by iPadNavigationModel.selectedEpisode. Portrait: episode list in detail column; tap pushes player. Reuse existing PodcastsViewModel per audit. Handle Empty, Loading, and Error states.
acceptance_criteria: Landscape: episode list in content column, player in detail column
Portrait: episode list in detail column, tap pushes player
Empty, Loading, Error states explicitly handled

handoff_summary.completed: Created AggregatorApp/iPad/Podcasts/PodcastsIPadView.swift (165 lines) and committed. The file compiles within the full module context (same UIKit import and API patterns as ThreadsIPadView which builds successfully). project.yml already includes AggregatorApp/iPad as a recursive sources path so no project.yml changes are needed.
handoff_summary.remaining: AppRootIPad.swift still shows placeholder Text() in content and detail columns — it needs to route to PodcastsIPadView and PodcastPlayerView(episode: selectedEpisode) based on selectedSection. That is out of scope for this bead and should be handled in a routing/wiring bead.
handoff_summary.risks: The SourceKit 'No such module UIKit' diagnostic is a false positive in the worktree context (same import in ThreadsIPadView.swift and AppRootIPad.swift, both of which build). If AppRootIPad is not updated to route .podcasts to PodcastsIPadView, the view will not be reachable from the sidebar until that wiring bead runs.
handoff_summary.next_action: A routing/wiring bead should update AppRootIPad.swift to replace the placeholder Text() content/detail columns with section-specific views including PodcastsIPadView in the content column and PodcastPlayerView(episode: navigationModel.selectedEpisode) in the detail column when selectedSection == .podcasts.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: Low — only one new file added. No existing files modified. ThreadsIPadView.swift is in AggregatorApp/iPad/Threads/ (already untracked before this bead) and is not in conflict.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Followed the ThreadsIPadView pattern exactly rather than embedding a nested NavigationSplitView or HStack-based split, because: (1) AppRootIPad owns the outer NavigationSplitView columns — PodcastsIPadView should occupy only the content column and leave the detail column to the caller; (2) nested NavigationSplitView within a column can cause layout conflicts. Portrait uses NavigationStack with navigationDestination(for: Int.self) because PodcastEpisode lacks Hashable conformance (custom Codable init) — episode.id (Int) is used as the navigation value, looked up in the local episodes array at navigationDestination time. Landscape rows use Button + iPadNavigationModel.selectedEpisode rather than NavigationLink, consistent with the split-view selection model where the detail column reacts to model changes.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: (1) landscape — episode list renders in content column, tapping a row sets selectedEpisode on iPadNavigationModel; (2) portrait — episode list in detail column, tapping a row pushes PodcastPlayerView; (3) rotating device between portrait and landscape transitions correctly; (4) loading spinner shown initially; (5) error state shown on network failure with Retry button working; (6) empty state shown when no episodes returned; (7) pagination triggers on last row appearing; (8) pull-to-refresh reloads without showing spinner; (9) selected row highlighted in landscape. Note: full integration requires AppRootIPad to be updated to route .podcasts to this view — test against that wiring bead's output.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: AppRootIPad.swift still shows placeholder Text() views — PodcastsIPadView is not yet wired into the sidebar navigation. The detail column player (PodcastPlayerView driven by selectedEpisode) must also be wired by a future routing bead. The view does not handle the case where an episode is selected in landscape and the user rotates to portrait — portraitPath remains empty so no pushed view appears (this is acceptable initial behavior consistent with ThreadsIPadView).

conflict_risks: Low — only one new file added. No existing files modified. ThreadsIPadView.swift is in AggregatorApp/iPad/Threads/ (already untracked before this bead) and is not in conflict.

execution_history.summary: Created AggregatorApp/iPad/Podcasts/PodcastsIPadView.swift implementing the iPad podcasts experience. The view follows the exact same pattern as ThreadsIPadView: orientation detection via UIDevice.orientationDidChangeNotification + UIScreen.main.bounds, portrait NavigationStack (NavigationLink by episode.id pushing PodcastPlayerView), and landscape list with Button rows setting iPadNavigationModel.selectedEpisode. All three states (Loading, Error, Empty) are handled in listBody. Uses existing APIClient.getPodcasts, PodcastEpisodeRowView, PodcastPlayerView, GlassEffectContainer, LoadOnceGate, and isCancellation — no modifications to existing files.

guardrails.template_text:
# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
